questions.explain: DMA catches the known-knowns deterministically; the LLM scan of sys.sql_modules catches patterns no rule was written for, with humans reviewing every flagged object.
options: It runs DBCC CHECKDB on the target server

It feeds every module definition from sys.sql_modules to an LLM alongside the target version's breaking-change list, producing CLEAN/REVIEW/BROKEN verdicts per object — tuned for recall, since missed BROKENs cost more than false REVIEWs
It asks developers to self-report issues
It compares backup file sizes between versions
questions.q: How does the chapter's AI compatibility assessment work?

questions.explain: The automated loop catches syntax errors and changed result shapes; the model's changes/notes arrays then guide human review of semantic judgment calls.
options: Running the rewrite directly in production and watching for errors
Peer review by two developers with no testing
SET NOEXEC ON parse check plus sys.dm_exec_describe_first_result_set result-shape comparison, executed in a scratch database against a schema-only copy — before any human review
Comparing line counts of old and new code
questions.q: What verification loop makes LLM T-SQL conversion trustworthy?

questions.explain: An object with forty dependents needing a semantic rewrite is not a one-hour task; the dependency-weighted classification makes the estimate defensible and the verdict burn-down honest.
options: By classifying every object by remediation complexity and weighting by dependency depth from sys.sql_expression_dependencies — with the burn-down of REVIEW/BROKEN verdicts as the progress metric
By gut feel in a planning meeting
By counting tables
By the size of the backup files
questions.q: How should migration effort be estimated according to the chapter?

questions.explain: Forty regressions become a handful of clusters, each with pre/post durations, I/O deltas, and wait categories as evidence for the model's triage.
options: One by one, in no particular order
By clustering regressed queries around the @cutover timestamp by dominant wait category and table set, then having the LLM propose a likely cause and first action per cluster
By rolling back immediately on any regression
By disabling Query Store after the upgrade
questions.q: How does the chapter triage post-upgrade Query Store regressions?

questions.explain: The draft's value is completeness (never forgetting to re-enable ETL jobs); it is a starting point for red-lining, not an executable plan, and it improves via accumulated corrections.
options: It executes the upgrade steps automatically
It replaces the runbook with a chatbot
It emails the runbook to management
It drafts an environment-specific runbook from inventory — AG topology, Agent jobs, compat levels, assessment verdicts — which a senior DBA red-lines; corrections feed back into the prompt template
questions.q: What is the AI's role in producing the upgrade runbook?
